policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 1:1 reads 'an apostle of Christ Jesus', the order Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ; the transposed Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ would give 'Jesus Christ'.
ASV 1:1 reads 'and Christ Jesus our hope': the order is Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ and there is no 'Lord', so the longer κυριόυ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ is excluded on both counts.
ASV 1:2 reads 'from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord'; 'our' attaches to Lord alone, with no 'our Father', so the added ἡμῶν after πατρὸς is not rendered.

ASV 1:4 'which minister questionings' renders ἐκζητήσεις and the simplex ζητήσεις identically; the only note on the verse is an alternative_rendering about 'dispensation/stewardship' and does not touch this word.

ASV 1:12 opens 'I thank him that enabled me' with no connective; the ASV renders sentence-initial καί, so the absence of 'And' points to Χάριν without καί. The verse's textual_variant note ('read enableth') concerns the participle's tense, not this conjunction.
ASV 1:13 'though I was before a blasphemer' leaves the article's case invisible in English; τὸ πρότερον and τὸν πρότερον ὄντα yield the same rendering and no note is mapped here.
ASV 1:16 reads 'might Jesus Christ show forth', the order Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, against the base Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς.
ASV 1:16 'all his longsuffering' renders ἅπασαν and πᾶσαν alike; the ASV marks no intensive force for ἅπας here.
ASV 1:17 reads 'the only God' with no 'wise'; the added σοφῷ would be rendered ('the only wise God'), and the verse's three notes are greek_gloss only.
ASV 1:18 'that by them thou mayest war the good warfare' does not distinguish present στρατεύῃ from aorist στρατεύσῃ; English 'mayest war' serves either aspect.
